source: visualnovel CLAUDE.md, Comments + Prose sections (2026-08-24 snapshot)

rules.name: comment-describes-code-below
rules.desc: A comment placed above an if/branch must describe that branch, not the opposite case; misplacement is a correctness bug.

rules.name: no-commented-out-code
rules.desc: Commented-out code (a call, import, or block) must be deleted, not kept as commentary.

rules.name: no-restate-code
rules.desc: A comment must not restate what the code already says; it must give a reason, constraint, or consequence.

rules.name: cite-named-constant
rules.desc: A comment should cite a named constant's identifier rather than hardcoding its value in prose.

rules.name: rename-not-comment
rules.desc: If a comment exists only to translate a bad identifier's meaning, rename the identifier instead of commenting it.

rules.name: comment-consequence-not-arguments
rules.desc: A comment on a call site should say what the call does to the surroundings, not restate arguments already visible on screen.

rules.name: state-facts-not-defend-design
rules.desc: A comment should state facts a reader could not derive (ordering constraint, platform quirk, live alternative), not defend or justify the design ('why this is the good version').

rules.name: doc-comment-continues-declaration
rules.desc: A doc comment continues its declaration grammatically; it must not re-supply the subject or narrate the signature.

rules.name: inline-vs-doc-punctuation
rules.desc: An inline // note is an unpunctuated fragment; a /** */ doc comment is a punctuated sentence. Don't mix the conventions.

rules.name: non-doc-comment-slashes
rules.desc: Non-doc comments use //, not /* */.

rules.name: non-doc-comment-length
rules.desc: Non-doc comments are at most 3 lines except rare, genuinely load-bearing context.

rules.name: doc-comment-concise
rules.desc: Doc comments say what the thing is and any non-obvious contract; they don't restate the signature or narrate the implementation.

rules.name: no-non-latin1-unicode
rules.desc: A comment must not contain a Unicode codepoint above U+00FF (outside Latin-1) unless it is covered by the project's unicodeWhitelist config.

rules.name: no-epigrams
rules.desc: Prose must be plain and declarative, not an epigram or aphorism that needs a second read to parse.

rules.name: no-inverted-syntax-personification
rules.desc: The sentence must inform, not perform; avoid inverted syntax and personification.

rules.name: no-metaphorical-equations
rules.desc: Avoid 'X is Y' / 'X as Y' metaphorical equations ('the leak scan is the refusal'); say what happens instead.

rules.name: no-fragment-opener
rules.desc: Do not name a placeholder and then withhold the real content behind a colon or dash ('The redactor to scan a report with: ...'). Lead with a complete sentence.

rules.name: no-double-negatives
rules.desc: State the positive claim instead of a double negative ('cannot be relied on not to').

rules.name: no-dangling-reference
rules.desc: Avoid pronouns/ellipses that point outside the sentence ('the second case', 'asking twice is how...'); each sentence should carry its own referents.

rules.name: no-clause-a-else-b
rules.desc: Avoid 'Resolve X: the named case when it exists, else the other case' constructions; spell out each case as its own ordinary sentence.

rules.name: no-trailing-adverb-on-noun-phrase
rules.desc: Avoid an adverb hung off the end of a noun phrase ('the next pointerdown anywhere'); attach the qualification to a verb or state it as its own fact.

rules.name: no-nonassertive-under-definite
rules.desc: Avoid 'any/anywhere/ever' modifying a definite description that names exactly one thing.

rules.name: no-rhetorical-emphasis
rules.desc: Avoid bold/italic markup inside a sentence to mark emphasis; put the load-bearing claim first as plain text.

rules.name: accurate-head-noun
rules.desc: The sentence's head noun must be what the thing actually is; don't assert it's an X and then retract that through a preposition ('as commands').

rules.name: backticks-for-code-only
rules.desc: Backticks are reserved for code symbols (identifiers, types, commands, file globs), not for a path or reference cited in prose.

rules.name: bracket-not-comma-alternative
rules.desc: A subordinate alternative should be parenthesized, not fenced with paired commas which create ambiguity about clause boundaries.

rules.name: bracket-supporting-premise
rules.desc: A clause that only supports a following 'so'/'therefore' conclusion must be bracketed or attached as a relative clause, not coordinated with 'and' as a peer assertion in the chain. The checker fires on one sub-case: the coordinated clause opens with a pronoun ('it', 'they', 'neither', ...) that continues the previous clause's subject.

rules.name: bracket-not-dash-interpolation
rules.desc: An interpolation fenced with paired dashes should be parenthesized or made its own sentence; paired dashes leave the clause boundaries as ambiguous as paired commas do.
